identity.title: AGN Feedback and Star Formation of Quasar Host Galaxies: Insights from the Molecular Gas

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use CO(2–1) observations from a new ALMA survey, in conjunction with literature measurements, to investigate the molecular gas properties of a representative sample of 40 $z < 0.3$ Palomar-Green quasars

As a follow-up to (cite: Shangguan2020ApJS), the main goals of the current paper are to search for evidence of quasar-mode AGN feedback and to investigate the AGN-starburst connection in quasar host galaxies.

question.value: Does AGN feedback affect the molecular gas and star formation of low-redshift PG quasar host galaxies, and how is AGN activity linked to the molecular gas?

analysis_steps.goal: Search for outflow emission and set upper limits

method.value: Continuum-subtracted cubes; combine channels -1000 to -500 and +500 to +1000 km/s; measure flux in 10'' aperture; 3σ limit from source-free areas

evidence.quote: we place a $3\,\sigma$ upper limit on high-velocity emission from the intensity map generated by combining the velcity channels between $-1000$ to $-500\, \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and $+500$ to $+1000\, \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$

assumptions.value: R21 = 0.62 and alpha_CO = 0.8 for outflow mass

evidence.quote: We adopt $R_{21}=0.62$ (cite: Shangguan2019ApJ) and $\alpha_\mathrm{CO}=0.8$
We then fit the visibility data with the CASA task `uvmodelfit` using a two-dimensional Gaussian model.

validation.value: Simulations with simobserve show robust sizes for >1''; consistent within 30% with high-resolution ALMA radii for six quasars

evidence.quote: the CO radii constrained from the ACA data are consistent within 30% of the half-light radii measured by J. Molina et al. (in preparation)

analysis_steps.goal: Derive gas masses, stellar masses and correlations

method.value: Kendall tau with censored data (cenken), Linmix and LTS_PLANEFIT fits, partial correlation

evidence.quote: We use the generalized Kendall’s $\tau$ calculated with the `cenken` function from the NADA package of `R`
assuming a CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor of $\alpha_\mathrm{CO} = 3.1$

claims.hypothesis: Quasar feedback quenches star formation or removes cold gas
claims.experiment: CO(2–1) ACA survey, outflow search, Tully-Fisher, gas masses, SFR
claims.result: Gas-rich, regular kinematics, no outflows, SFR above main sequence
claims.finding: No sign of AGN feedback quenching star formation

evidence.quote: There is no sign that AGN feedback quenches star formation for the quasars in our sample.

claims.hypothesis: L_IR–AGN luminosity correlation reflects AGN influence
claims.experiment: Partial correlation removing dependence on L'CO and M_BH
claims.finding: Correlation driven by common molecular gas dependence

evidence.quote: The observed strong correlation between host galaxy total infrared luminosity and AGN luminosity arises from their common dependence on the molecular gas.

limitations_admitted.value: Partial correlation may need a much larger sample; outflow limits depend on alpha_CO and radius

evidence.quote: One caveat, however, is that revealing a statistically significant partial correlation may require a sample much larger than that considered here

referee_caveats_inferred: Indirect stellar masses uncertain by 0.65 dex
